title: Launch lane reservation marketplace and capacity-sweep protocol for mixed-runtime model rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple product teams compete for limited Dedicated and Private capacity during overlapping rollout windows (model updates, quantization rollouts, console changes). Current ad-hoc reservation practices cause last-minute throttle, missed SLAs, and emergency capacity purchases.

Goal: Design and ship a lightweight "launch lane reservation marketplace" plus an automated pre-launch "capacity sweep" that: (1) lets PMs reserve capacity lanes with priority/credits, (2) publishes a canonical launch calendar that integrates Dedicated capacity forecasts, and (3) runs an automated sweep pre-cutover to verify guardrails and trigger fallbacks. The feature should support mixed-runtime rollouts (hosted + dedicated + private), model-impacting changes (quantize, kernel swaps), and region-aware blackout windows.

Success metrics: adoption by >= 4 internal product teams for Q2 launches, reduce emergency capacity spend by 40% for weeks with major launches, and decrease last-minute rollback incidents tied to capacity constraints to < 1 per quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation UI/API: teams can create lane reservations with start/end times, capacity units, priority level and optional backup lane
Calendar integration: reservations appear on centralized launch calendar and expose conflicts with automated recommend/resolution hints
Capacity sweep: automated pre-launch validation job that verifies node availability, model variant compatibility and fallback policies 48/6/1 hours before cutover
Fallback automation: if sweep fails, policy engine automatically triggers pre-configured fallback (lower-tier model, region failover, or cutover rollback) and notifies stakeholders
Audit trail: reservation lifecycle events are logged to Private audit logs and Console timeline for postmortems
milestones: Spec and stakeholder alignment (Feb 10 - Feb 18): completed
API + calendar prototype (Feb 19 - Feb 28): design + lightweight backend contract
Capacity sweep job PoC (Mar 01 - Mar 10): runtime integration and sweep checks
Canary with one product team (Mar 11 - Mar 21): end-to-end reservation, sweep, fallback exercises
General availability and runbook (Mar 25): docs, SDK snippets, and oncall playbook
